{"grade":6,"complete":false,"main_gap":"The set Q is wrongly defined as primes dividing A; the proof requires Q to be all primes at most A.","errors":[{"description":"With the stated Q, it is false that all prime factors at most A lie in σ(x), or that primes outside σ(x) exceed A. Thus the key lemma and periodicity (3) fail. Indeed, the write-up’s A=15 example gives selected 18 and skipped 21 with identical stated σ. Replacing Q by all primes at most A repairs the proof.","quote":"Let
\[
Q=\{p:p\text{ is prime and }p\mid A\},
\qquad
\sigma(x)=P(x)\cap Q.
\]"}],"notes":"The intended correction is evident from later statements and is a single definitional change; after it, the induction and translation-periodicity argument are complete."}
